Trustworthy Evaluation of AI-Assisted Painting Restoration

Stable Diffusion Inpainting

Evaluation status: fully_evaluated. This report summarizes validated Notebook 09–30 evidence and creates no new scientific evidence.

Executive Summary

This standalone report evaluates Stable Diffusion Inpainting using validated restoration, metric, robustness, uncertainty, failure, explanation, and compute evidence.

Evaluation statusfully_evaluatedComplete scope
Paintings50410 cases
Candidates1330955 with explanation-catalog coverage
First-place anchors0/11core_three_model
Mean runtime9.225 sRecorded local system
Flagged candidates955/955At least one triggered trustworthiness flag
Thesis alignment: RQ1, RQ2, and RQ3: model quality, conditional behaviour, and support for human review.

What the evidence shows

  • Evaluation status: fully_evaluated.
  • Coverage: 50 paintings, 410 cases, and 1330 candidates.
  • Observed mean runtime: 9.225 seconds per candidate on the recorded system.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting ranked third and was worse overall than the two deterministic methods under the approved family-balanced evaluation.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Unmeasured physical-conservation outcomes remain inconclusive.

1. Method Identity

This section defines what the evaluated method is, what role it can reasonably serve, and where that role ends.

Field Value
Model family Prompt Conditioned Latent Diffusion Inpainting
Methodological role Prompt Conditioned Stochastic Inpainting Baseline
Implementation Diffusers StableDiffusionInpaintPipeline
Model identifier stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-inpainting
Deterministic False
Prompt dependent True
Execution device cuda
Precision float16

Intended uses

  • prompt-conditioned generative inpainting baseline
  • repeated-seed variability analysis
  • controlled prompt-sensitivity analysis for thin scratches

Excluded uses

  • historically verified reconstruction
  • calibrated confidence estimation
  • unreviewed conservation decisions
Thesis alignment: RQ3: defines the model's appropriate role in a human-centred evaluation workflow.

What the evidence shows

  • Strengths: prompt-conditioned generative completion; seed-controllable stochastic candidates; supports empirical variability analysis.
  • Weaknesses: high hallucination and prompt-sensitivity risk; higher compute and candidate multiplier; thin-mask geometry can remain visible after compositing.
  • Intended uses: prompt-conditioned generative inpainting baseline; repeated-seed variability analysis; controlled prompt-sensitivity analysis for thin scratches.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting is better treated as prompt conditioned stochastic inpainting baseline than as an autonomous restoration authority.
Limitation: The evaluated implementation and configuration do not establish historically authentic recovery.

3. Overall Quality Evidence

Eleven transparent quality anchors combine classical, perceptual, feature, spatial, local, semantic, and structural evidence. Lower plotted rank is better.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: compares restoration quality using transparent complementary evidence.

What the evidence shows

  • The model ranked first on 0 of 11 transparent quality anchors in its approved comparison population.
  • Family-balanced baseline rank: 3 of three complete-scope methods.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting ranked third and was worse overall than the two deterministic methods under the approved family-balanced evaluation.
Limitation: Ranks summarize metric-defined behaviour; they do not prove historical correctness or universal model superiority.

4. Damage Types and Experiments

This section keeps damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, and synthetic-degradation evidence separate. Positive adverse slopes indicate worse restoration behaviour under the stated exposure.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: tests whether behaviour changes with damage size, mask geometry, and synthetic degradation.

What the evidence shows

  • Damage-size deterioration was confirmed on 4 of 11 anchors.
  • 7 of 11 damage-size intervals crossed zero and remain inconclusive.
  • Synthetic-degradation severity produced 18 adverse and 15 opposite-direction metric-family summaries.
Conclusion: Larger damage made Stable Diffusion Inpainting worse on 4 anchors with intervals entirely above zero. The remaining 7 anchors do not support a directional claim. Synthetic degradation was mixed rather than uniformly better or worse.
Limitation: Extension experiments contain five paintings for the core models. Metric-native slope sizes cannot be compared directly across different anchors.

5. Texture, Colour, and Seam Behaviour

Local texture, colour, and seam diagnostics test whether a plausible-looking repair remains visibly inconsistent near or inside the restored region.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and approved local-consistency extension: evaluates defects missed by global similarity.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place local anchors: 0 of three.
  • The three anchors cover local texture error, masked colour difference, and boundary-seam mismatch.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting was not best on any of the three local anchors and was worse than at least one comparator for texture, colour, and seam evidence.
Limitation: Each anchor measures a different failure mode; their numerical scales are not interchangeable.

6. Semantic and Structural Evidence

Semantic and structural measurements test local content and organization beyond pixel similarity. They remain proxies rather than proof of historical meaning.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and the semantic/XAI extension: evaluates whether local structure and meaning are preserved.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place semantic or structural anchors: 0 of three.
  • The evidence covers local semantic DINO, structural affinity, and structural SSIM.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting was not best on any semantic or structural anchor and was worse than at least one core comparator on each.
Limitation: Feature agreement does not establish iconographic correctness, artist intent, or historical truth.

7. Uncertainty, Prompt, and Stability Evidence

Uncertainty is treated as empirical repeated-seed variability only. Deterministic methods and insufficient seed coverage are reported as not applicable.

Thesis alignment: RQ2 and uncertainty extension: distinguishes stochastic sensitivity from restoration quality.

What the evidence shows

  • 165 complete four-seed uncertainty groups were retained.
  • They comprise 130 canonical groups and 35 damage-size groups.
  • Canonical evidence retains generic and scratch-aware prompt arms without mixing them.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion is better suited than the deterministic methods to empirical seed-variability analysis because repeated candidates exist. However, low variability is not proof of a better or correct restoration.
Limitation: Empirical variability is not calibrated confidence and does not measure historical correctness.

9. Difference and Explanation Maps

These panels pair restored outputs with available difference, uncertainty, semantic, texture, colour, seam, or boundary diagnostics. Bright or intense regions must be interpreted using each map's stated scale.

Thesis alignment: RQ3 and XAI extension: supports localized human review rather than opaque acceptance.

What the evidence shows

  • 18 diagnostic-map tiles are embedded beside representative cases.
  • Maps are drawn from validated spatial, local, uncertainty, and semantic manifests where applicable.
Conclusion: The maps are better than scalar metrics alone for locating where a restoration changed or failed. They do not establish why the generated content is historically correct.
Limitation: Map colour and intensity remain specific to each diagnostic definition and scale.

10. Failure Taxonomy and Trustworthiness Flags

Failure categories describe observed metric-defined patterns. Trustworthiness flags convert supported patterns into auditable review actions.

Recommendation Candidates
Do Not Rely Automatically 130
Specialist Review Required 794
Suitable For Preliminary Inspection 1
Unstable Candidate 30
Thesis alignment: RQ3: turns multiple diagnostic failures into auditable human-review actions.

What the evidence shows

  • The trustworthiness catalog covers 955 candidates.
  • At least one flag was triggered for 955 candidates.
  • Critical flags affected 395 candidates; warning flags affected 955.
Conclusion: Triggered flags mean automated reliance would be worse than specialist review for the affected candidates. A flag is a screening signal, not a final conservation verdict.
Limitation: Some flag families are unavailable or only partially supported for particular candidates.

11. Compute and Scalability

Observed execution evidence and the transparent 300-painting projection are shown separately.

Evidence Population Runtime Status
Observed complete evaluated run 50 paintings / 1330 candidates 3.41 hours executed
300-painting canonical-primary projection 300 paintings / 1,500 candidates 3.24 hours central estimate projection, not executed
Thesis alignment: Approved compute extension: evaluates practical deployment and scaling feasibility.

What the evidence shows

  • Observed mean runtime: 9.225 seconds per candidate.
  • Observed p95 runtime: 10.149 seconds.
  • Projected central runtime for 300 paintings under the canonical-primary design: 3.24 hours.
  • Projected report-owned restoration storage: 1042.0 MiB.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting was slower than the fastest evaluated method on the recorded system. This is a compute disadvantage, not a quality conclusion.
Limitation: Observed timings describe one workstation. The 300-painting runtime and storage values were not executed experiments.

12. Decision Support

Strengths

  • prompt-conditioned generative completion
  • seed-controllable stochastic candidates
  • supports empirical variability analysis

Weaknesses

  • high hallucination and prompt-sensitivity risk
  • higher compute and candidate multiplier
  • thin-mask geometry can remain visible after compositing
Thesis alignment: RQ3: translates evidence into a bounded human-review recommendation.

What the evidence shows

  • Main strengths: prompt-conditioned generative completion; seed-controllable stochastic candidates; supports empirical variability analysis.
  • Main weaknesses: high hallucination and prompt-sensitivity risk; higher compute and candidate multiplier; thin-mask geometry can remain visible after compositing.
Conclusion: Stable Diffusion Inpainting is better used within its declared role and worse when extended to excluded uses. Its outputs require comparison with the clean reference, local diagnostics, flags, and expert judgement.
Limitation: The report supports prioritization and review; it does not authorize treatment of a physical artwork.

13. Limitations

The limitations below are retained from the canonical model card and evidence contract.

  • Runtime and memory observations describe one recorded local workstation and software environment.
  • The 300-painting values are transparent linear projections, not executed experiments.
  • Projected storage covers notebook-owned output artifacts and excludes model caches, environments, Git history, and downstream metric outputs.
  • SDXL has ten completed candidates nested within five paintings and cannot support a full-scope ranking.
  • LaMa per-case runtime includes transparent allocation from IOPaint batch wall-clock measurements.
  • Quality-anchor wins are descriptive validated Notebook 21 evidence, not a universal quality or conservation score.
  • Stable Diffusion produces plausible prompt-conditioned inpainting, not historically verified reconstruction.
  • The generic primary prompt and fixed inference settings are intentionally not tuned per painting or damage case.
  • Contextual prompts form a controlled ablation and are not used to select primary candidates.
  • Repeated seeds characterize stochastic sensitivity for a fixed predeclared subset and are not metric-selected.
  • Eligible synthetic-degradation cases are supplementary masked-removal diagnostics and remain separate from missing-content claims.
  • CUDA inference may not be byte-identical across hardware or software stacks; the complete environment is recorded.
  • The safety checker is disabled for this fixed research dataset and that policy is explicitly recorded.
  • The scratch-aware prompt is a controlled semantic-conditioning treatment and does not change the model, mask, seed, scheduler, inference resolution, compositing policy, or any other generation setting.
  • Thin scratch masks can lose or fragment spatial support during 512-pixel and latent-grid downsampling; prompting cannot be assumed to resolve that geometric limitation.
  • Literal scratch terminology is concentrated in the negative prompt because text encoders may not reliably interpret negation in positive prompts.
  • The 200 painting-seed pairs are repeated observations nested within 50 paintings; downstream inference must not treat all seed-level pairs as independent paintings.
Thesis alignment: RQ1–RQ3: defines what the evaluation does and does not establish.

What the evidence shows

  • Excluded uses: historically verified reconstruction; calibrated confidence estimation; unreviewed conservation decisions.
  • 17 persisted model and evaluation limitations are retained from the model card.
Conclusion: The evidence can identify comparatively better or worse metric-defined behaviour, while historical authenticity and physical conservation suitability remain inconclusive.
Limitation: Synthetic damage, digital references, model-domain gaps, and incomplete human evidence constrain every claim.
